correctness.rationale: Each time slice is a two-term polynomial in an L-th root of unity. It has either 0 or d zeros when both endpoints are occupied, with d zeros exactly on a good internal edge. Path components permit all internal edges to be good. A full odd cycle cannot make all L edges good because their root-of-unity ratios would multiply to -1, while L-1 good edges are attained by alternating signs. Summing slice supports yields the formula. The global minimum follows from the exact component contributions. Exhaustive integer replay checks all supports through N=12 and the global component formula for all parameter pairs through N=5000.

value.rationale: Fixed-window STFT concentration is a natural refinement of the universal finite-group uncertainty principle. The canonical two-point window is the simplest nongeneric sparse window, and the theorem gives a closed all-N answer for every prescribed signal support, exposing an exact odd-cycle obstruction and the sharp antipodal/non-antipodal transition. This supplies a reusable benchmark for sparse-window Gabor localization rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
